title: E. coli and B. subtilis Colony PCR
author: Igem Dusseldorf
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8fhhtj6

steps.title: Prepare PCR master mix
steps.instruction: In a sterile tube combine 72 µL sterile MilliQ water, 90 µL Red Taq 2× Master Mix (1.5 mM MgCl₂), 9 µL forward primer (10 µM), and 9 µL reverse primer (10 µM) to a total volume of 180 µL (sufficient for 9 reactions, 20 µL each).

substeps.instruction: Add 90 µL Red Taq 2× Master Mix (1.5 mM MgCl₂).
Mix gently and keep on ice.

steps.title: Aliquot master mix into tubes
steps.instruction: Dispense 20 µL of the prepared master mix into each of 8 PCR tubes of a strip.

steps.title: Add colony cells to reactions
steps.instruction: Using a sterile P2 pipette tip or inoculating loop, transfer cells from a single colony into each tube (8 colonies total).

steps.title: Run thermocycler program
steps.instruction: Place the strip in a thermocycler and run the following program (suitable for a 1.5 kb insert): initial denaturation at 95 °C for 3 min; then 25 cycles of 95 °C for 20 s, 57 °C for 30 s, and 72 °C for 5 min; finish with a hold at 64 °C (infinite).

steps.title: Electrophorese PCR products on gel
steps.instruction: Load the PCR samples onto an agarose gel and run at 80–150 V until the loading dye front reaches approximately 75–80 % of the gel length (typically 1–1.5 h, depending on gel concentration and voltage).
